title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 27 (Court assistance in taking evidence)

content.overview: The arbitral tribunal, or a party with the approval of the tribunal, may apply to the Court for assistance in taking evidence. The Court may execute the request within its competence and according to its rules on taking evidence, including directing that evidence be provided directly to the tribunal.
content.glance: Tribunal (or party with tribunal approval) may seek Court assistance in taking evidence; Court executes within its competence.
content.study: The tribunal, or a party with tribunal approval, may apply to the Court for assistance in taking evidence. The Court executes the request within its competence and rules on taking evidence and may direct that evidence be provided directly to the tribunal.

sections.heading: Who may apply
sections.body: Tribunal, or a party with the approval of the tribunal.

sections.heading: Court assistance
sections.body: Court executes the request within its competence and rules on taking evidence.

sections.heading: Direct provision to tribunal
sections.body: Court may direct that evidence be provided directly to the arbitral tribunal.
